summary: The English of all six mishnayot is accurate and follows Bartenura and Rambam; it needs only one real repair, the gloss of נִפְרָעִין (3:16), which is 'they collect payment', not 'they are exacted'. The main faults are in the token data: senses were filled mechanically (sense 1 everywhere, including part-of-speech labels and etymologies), and many default lexicon keys are wrong homographs (Torah as 'custom', Akiva as 'heel', Adam, Tob, Rosh, Sheresh, Dan) where the pack lists the right entry. Some summaries misread their comment (Bartenura 3:14:1 and 3:17:3; Rambam 3:13:1 is recorded, not followed), the 3:18 grammar note calls תְּקוּפוֹת Greek, and the 3:17 Vilna variants were left out. The model morphology has eleven wrong analyses, chiefly בַּצֹּרֶת split as בְּ + צֹרֶת, the participles נִדּוֹן and בָּאָה parsed as perfects, and wrong genders.

patches.value: אֵין is the negative existential particle: 'there is not', 'there is no'. The conditional pairs אִם אֵין ... אֵין ... are mirror statements: each term is a condition for the other. The pack's key bdbs:אַיִן is the homograph 'where?' (אַיִן interrogative), not the negative אֵין; this holds for every אֵין in the mishnah, and no sense is given.

value: The first part is four mirror-image pairs of conditionals אִם אֵין X, אֵין Y / אִם אֵין Y, אֵין X: each of Torah and proper conduct, wisdom and fear, understanding and knowledge, flour and Torah depends on the other. The English keeps the repetition, because the symmetry is the argument.
אֵין is the negative existential particle, not a verb: 'there is not'. In a conditional with אִם: 'if there is no X, there is no Y'.

The second saying is introduced by הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר and has two parallel images (tree with many branches and few roots; tree with few branches and many roots), each with the same structure: כָּל שֶׁ... לְמַה הוּא דוֹמֶה, לְאִילָן שֶׁ..., then a proof text. The English keeps the repeated question.
מְרֻבָּה, מְרֻבִּין, מֻעָטִין are Pual participles ('are increased, are decreased'), used as predicate adjectives; the passive implies natural growth.

וְהָרוּחַ בָּאָה וְעוֹקַרְתּוֹ וְהוֹפַכְתּוֹ עַל פָּנָיו: three feminine participles (בָּאָה, then two Qal participles with object suffixes) in a series; the image is told in the present, 'the wind comes and uproots it and overturns it'. In the second image the verbs are participles too: בָּאוֹת וְנוֹשְׁבוֹת, 'coming and blowing'.
Both proof texts are from Jeremiah 17: the first (verse 6) is about 'the one who trusts in man'; the second (verse 8) about 'the one who trusts in the LORD'. The mishnah quotes only the images.
patches.reason: בָּאָה in a series with the participles וְעוֹקַרְתּוֹ וְהוֹפַכְתּוֹ is the feminine participle (stress on the last syllable), not the perfect; the English 'comes' already reads it so.

patches.value: Bartenura: דַּעַת is finding the reason for a thing; בִּינָה is understanding one thing from another without being able to show its reason (אֵינוֹ מַרְאֶה לוֹ טַעַם). Without knowledge to give the reason there is no understanding, for not knowing the reason is like not knowing the thing; yet understanding comes first, so without understanding there is no knowledge.
patches.reason: אֵינוֹ מַרְאֶה לוֹ טַעַם: the one who has בִּינָה cannot show the reason; the summary said he is not shown it.

value: Jeremiah 17:6 (וְהָיָה כְּעַרְעָר בָּעֲרָבָה וְלֹא יִרְאֶה כִּי יָבוֹא טוֹב וְשָׁכַן חֲרֵרִים בַּמִּדְבָּר אֶרֶץ מְלֵחָה וְלֹא תֵשֵׁב).

Jeremiah 17:8 (וְהָיָה כְּעֵץ שָׁתוּל עַל מַיִם וְעַל יוּבַל יְשַׁלַּח שָׁרָשָׁיו וְלֹא יִרְאֶה כִּי יָבֹא חֹם וְהָיָה עָלֵהוּ רַעֲנָן וּבִשְׁנַת בַּצֹּרֶת לֹא יִדְאָג וְלֹא יָמִישׁ מֵעֲשׂוֹת פֶּרִי).
Rabbeinu Yonah (3:17:5, 3:17:6) places knowledge before understanding; Bartenura says understanding comes first (אִם אֵין בִּינָה אֵין דַּעַת).

Vilna spells מרובה, מרובין, מועטין, יבא, שאפילו, חום and בצורת for מְרֻבָּה, מְרֻבִּין, מֻעָטִין, יָבוֹא, שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ, חֹם and בַּצֹּרֶת; in the citations it adds the verse number ו (Jeremiah 17:6) and reads ירמיה יז ח (Jeremiah 17:8) for שם.
patches.reason: The Vilna variants in the pack were not recorded; every witness's variants are to be kept.

patches.value: דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ: rendered 'proper conduct' because Bartenura and Rabbeinu Yonah both read it as decent behaviour toward people and good character traits in the first pair; in the pair about flour (קֶמַח) the same phrase could be read as 'worldly occupation', and I note that rather than change the word. The mishnah's יִרְאָה is 'fear', without 'of God', as in the Hebrew. For the pair דַּעַת / בִּינָה I follow Bartenura's distinction (דַּעַת 'finds the reason of a thing'; בִּינָה 'derives one thing from another'); the English uses the ordinary words 'knowledge' and 'understanding'. Rabbeinu Yonah describes the two differently (knowledge as what one grasps of oneself, understanding as inferring one thing from another). The pack's default lexicon keys for טוֹב, בָּא, דָּמָה, יוּבַל and צֹרֶת point to different words (a place, 'father', 'to cease', a proper name, a proper name); where the pack also lists the right entry (jastrow:טוֹב II, jastrow:דָּמָה ²) it is used, otherwise no sense is given and the correct word is read. Rambam's comment on דעת and בינה is anchored in the pack to 3:16.21 and is ruled on under 3:16.

value: Two sentences, each of two coordinated nouns followed by a predicate. The first has a doubled pronoun, הֵן הֵן, which marks emphasis: 'these, indeed these'. The second has no pronoun at all; the predicate is the single noun פַּרְפְּרָאוֹת.
קִנִּין is the plural of קֵן ('nest') used as a technical term for bird offerings. פִּתְחֵי נִדָּה is a construct chain, 'openings of the menstruant'.
גּוּפֵי הֲלָכוֹת is a construct chain: 'bodies of laws', meaning the core or essentials.

גִּימַטְרִיאוֹת and פַּרְפְּרָאוֹת are Greek loan words that the mishnah uses as technical terms; תְּקוּפוֹת is Hebrew, from the root קוף/נקף 'to go around' (Jastrow: 'turn, cycle'). The contrast of גּוּף ('body') with פַּרְפְּרָאוֹת ('after-dishes') is the point of the saying: the essential versus the ornamental.
patches.reason: תְּקוּפָה is a Hebrew noun from קוף 'to go around' (Jastrow, which the pack cites), not a Greek loan word. The doubled הֵן הֵן emphasises ('these very things', as the English has); 'only these' adds an exclusivity the Hebrew does not state.

patches.value: Two choices to record. פִּתְחֵי נִדָּה: the English keeps the literal 'the openings of the menstruant' because the sense of 'openings' is not simple (Bartenura: her opening or onset; Rabbeinu Yonah: three places in the house, and many appearances of blood). קִנִּין is rendered 'bird offerings' following Bartenura, with the literal 'nests' in the gloss. פַּרְפְּרָאוֹת is 'desserts' following Bartenura's image of the sweets eaten at the end of a meal, which continues the meal metaphor of the previous mishnah. The default Jastrow entry גּוּף I is the verb 'to squeeze'; the noun is jastrow:גּוּף II, sense 2 'essence'.
patches.reason: The note follows the corrected lexicon key.

patches.value: חִבָּה יְתֵרָה: 'extra love' (Jastrow: 'love'; יָתֵר 'surplus'). I keep 'extra' rather than 'special' to preserve the idea of a second, additional love beyond the first. נוֹדַעַת is read 'is made known' (Nifal of יָדַע) following Rambam as quoted by Bartenura: God informs the creature of the gift. The pack's BDB keys for טוֹב and אָדָם are proper names (Tob, Adam); the pack also lists jastrow:טוֹב II and jastrow:אָדָם, which give 'good' and 'man'. כְּלִי חֶמְדָּה is rendered 'a desirable vessel' to keep the biblical wording of חֶמְדָּה; the vessel is the Torah, by which the world was created. In Proverbs 4:2 תּוֹרָתִי can mean 'my teaching'; the English reads 'my Torah', as the mishnah applies the verse to the Torah.
patches.reason: The old note implied that the mishnah's wording of Proverbs 4:2 differs from the verse; it does not (both read תּוֹרָתִי). The lexicon sentence follows the corrected keys.

value: Genesis 9:6 (כִּי בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם).
Proverbs 4:2 (כִּי לֶקַח טוֹב נָתַתִּי לָכֶם תּוֹרָתִי אַל תַּעֲזֹבוּ).

Vilna reads יתירה, שניתן and תעזובו (spelling only) and ו for כִּי at 3:14.17; it also adds א and ב in the citations of Deuteronomy 14 and Proverbs 4. These are the verse numbers (Deuteronomy 14:1, Proverbs 4:2), not words of the text; the ו at 3:14.17 may likewise be the verse number of Genesis 9:6, aligned against כִּי.
patches.reason: The two variants without a token fall at the citations (דברים יד, משלי ד) and are the verse numbers 1 and 2, not extra words of the mishnah.

patches.value: Bartenura, citing Rambam: the Holy One showed the human being extra love by informing him that he was created in the image, for one who does a kindness and tells his friend of it shows more love than one who does it without telling. Another reading: נוֹדַעַת means a love that is revealed and public: not only a hidden love of the Omnipresent for the human being, but a love open and known to all.
patches.reason: Bartenura's second reading is חִבָּה גְּלוּיָה וּמְפֻרְסֶמֶת, a love revealed and known to all, not 'known to him through the verse'.

value.summary: Rambam: when a person vows and keeps his vows, he acquires the habit of holding back from what he wants to avoid, and separation (פְּרִישׁוּת) becomes easy for him; he takes פְּרִישׁוּת as guarding oneself from ritual impurity, as in 'the garments of an unlearned person are midras-impure for Perushim' (Hagigah 18b).

patches.reason: Rambam reads פְּרִישׁוּת as separation from ritual impurity; the English 'abstinence' follows Bartenura's self-restraint. Rambam's reading is a real alternative and is recorded, not followed.

patches.value: Rambam: 'everything is foreseen': all that is in the world is known to God; but foreknowledge does not compel, for 'the choice is given' to every person (his eighth chapter). God judges people with grace and goodness, not by the strict judgment due them. Virtues come according to the number (רֹב) of good deeds, not the size of one deed: a thousand coins given one at a time build generosity more than a thousand given at once.
patches.reason: The summary left out Rambam's reading of the last clause, which bears on the English 'abundance of deeds' (quantity, not magnitude).

patches.reason: בָּאָה stands in a series with the participles וְעוֹקַרְתּוֹ וְהוֹפַכְתּוֹ and is the feminine participle (stress on the last syllable), parallel to בָּאוֹת in the second image; the English 'comes' reads it so.
The root of עֵץ is עצה (BDB); 'עצ' is not a root (and lacks the final form).

בַּצֹּרֶת, 'drought' (Jer. 17:8; also Jer. 14:1), is one noun from בצר; the בּ is a root letter, not the preposition. בִּשְׁנַת בַּצֹּרֶת is 'in a year of drought'; Vilna's spelling בצורת confirms the one word.
הֵן here is the 3rd plural personal pronoun ('they'), doubled for emphasis and serving as the copula, not a demonstrative.
